Date: 2028-04-10T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: production alerts - auth errors rising

Kimberly / Redwood team —

Heads up: since ~08:00 PT we’re seeing a sharp spike in 5xxs on our auth endpoints that go through Redwood. Error rate ~15% at the 08:07 window (normally <0.5%). p95 latency for token-authorize has jumped from ~300ms to ~1.8s. Throughput from our side is steady but success traffic is dropping due to retries.

Attached are a few pulled traces (trace ids redacted) and a short sample of request IDs. We also see increased request queuing time reported in our client libraries.

This is impacting checkout flows for ~10% of our users. Can you activate a war-room? We need estimated time to stabilize and whether you can route us to a fallback model / region while you investigate.

Kevin

Early findings from us-west inference cluster:
- Observed a sudden spike in model-inference time on a quantized variant (v3-q4_8) for the token-authorize route starting 07:58 PT. Median backend latency for that variant jumped from ~200ms to ~950ms; queue depth tripled.
- GPU utilization for affected nodes is high, but not saturated; however there are long tail kernel stalls in the quantized execution path (see stack excerpt below).
- No autoscaler events yet; backlog is at the serving layer.

Immediate recommendation: roll traffic from v3-q4_8 -> v3-fp16-stable for this route (expected p95 reduction to ~350ms). I can perform a targeted rollback for the route with canary monitoring.

Attached: quant-runlog-us-west.txt (pulled lines) and a short command output. If we cannot roll safely, enable Dedicated burst capacity for the customer (temp) to relieve queue pressure.

Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Site Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference

- Canary 10% traffic on v3-fp16-stable for 5 minutes, then ramp if p95 and error rate improve.
- If rollback is insufficient, we will enable short-term burst capacity in us-west and route a fraction of traffic via our ue-central fallback region.

Subject: FastLane — final incident summary and executive readout

Sanjay / Kevin — final summary from the FastLane incident (Apr 10, 2028). Apologies again for the disruption and thank you for your partnership while we worked this. Below is an executive-readout and next steps.

Executive summary:
- Impact: the token-authorize route saw a transient error rate increase (peak ~15%) and p95 latency elevation (peak ~1.8s) between 07:58–09:05 PT on Apr 10. Impacted ~10% of checkout requests for FastLane production traffic during peak.
- Root cause: an edge-case regression in the quantized inference path for variant v3-q4_8 caused long-tail kernel stalls under specific input sequences. This surfaced as queue build-up in the us-west serving cluster.
- Mitigation applied: controlled rollback of route traffic to v3-fp16-stable and enabling temporary burst capacity for FastLane in us-west. Canary verification completed; p95 returned to baseline (≈320–360ms) and error rate dropped to <0.5% within ~28 minutes of mitigation.

Actions & commitments:
1) Immediate: we’ve disabled automatic rollout of v3-q4_8 to customer-facing routes until a full regression test is added to the onboarding pipeline (complete).
2) Short term (72h): engineering will run a focused playback across representative FastLane request traces to validate quantized execution and patch the kernel stall issue.
3) Compensation: Redwood will apply a one-time service credit for the impacted window; details in an emailed invoice addendum (payment/finance will follow up).
4) Executive sync: Naomi Feldman (Head of Customer Success) will coordinate a 30-minute postmortem with FastLane execs the week of Apr 16.

Attachments: latency graphs, the runlog snippet used during triage, and the SLA impact workbook are attached for your review.

We will share a technical postmortem with timelines and follow-through items by Apr 15. Please let us know a preferred time for the executive postmortem call.

Thank you again for the patience and for pausing batch jobs during the canary. 

Best regards —

Kimberly Park
